2609.27333.title: Alignment Inertia: Auditing the Durability of Training Data Influence Through Policy Override Resistance
2609.27333.paper_summary: Platform operators increasingly rely on system prompts and fine-tuning to govern model behavior, yet it remains unclear how reliably these interventions override behavior inherited from prior training. We propose Override Success Rate (OSR) and alignment inertia to measure when operator interventions succeed or fail to change prior behavior. We evaluate zero-shot prompting and LoRA fine-tuning across Llama and Mistral in medical misinformation and hate speech. Alignment inertia persists across both models but varies by model, domain, and policy direction. Notably, in Mistral's restrictive hate-speech condition, LoRA increased inertia by 46.5 percentage points, showing that fine-tuning can reinforce rather than override prior behavior. We also use TRAK to test whether inertia is associated with weaker adaptation signals. TRAK achieves AUC of at least 0.85 in 7 of 8 conditions and outperforms model confidence, TF-IDF similarity, and embedding similarity as a predictor of inertia. These results provide an operator-facing audit of where prior training constrains downstream model governance.
2609.27333.paper_summary_zh: 平台運營商越來越依賴系統提示和微調來管理模型行為，但這些干預措施在多大程度上能可靠地覆蓋從先前訓練中繼承的行為仍然不清楚。<lb/>我們提出了覆蓋成功率（OSR）和對齊慣性來衡量運營商干預何時成功或失敗地改變先前行為。<lb/>我們在醫療錯誤信息和仇恨言論中評估了零樣本提示和LoRA微調在Llama和Mistral上的效果。<lb/>對齊慣性在這兩個模型中持續存在，但因模型、領域和政策方向而異。<lb/>值得注意的是，在Mistral的限制性仇恨言論條件下，LoRA將慣性提高了46.5個百分點，顯示微調可以加強而不是覆蓋先前的行為。<lb/>我們還使用TRAK來測試慣性是否與較弱的適應信號相關。<lb/>TRAK在8個條件中的7個達到了至少0.85的AUC，並且在預測慣性方面超越了模型信心、TF-IDF相似度和嵌入相似度。<lb/>這些結果為運營商提供了一個審計，顯示先前的訓練如何限制下游模型治理。
